record.prompt: Please run scripts/cost.sh on data/orders-2026-10.tsv and tell me the total shipping cost for October. Don't edit the script or data/zone-rates.tsv.

base_changes.keywords: cost.sh, zone-rates.tsv, CRLF, no rate for zone, shipping cost, стоимость доставки
base_changes.content: scripts/cost.sh fails with 'no rate for zone "north"' because data/zone-rates.tsv has CRLF line endings (zone keys end in \r). Workaround without editing files: tr -d '\r' < data/zone-rates.tsv > /tmp/rates.tsv and pass it as the second argument: sh scripts/cost.sh ORDERS /tmp/rates.tsv.

record.final_answer:
The total shipping cost for October is **58.01**.

| Order | Zone | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A-1001 | north | 6.94 |
| A-1002 | south | 6.28 |
| A-1003 | island | 15.25 |
| A-1004 | north | 15.10 |
| A-1005 | south | 9.03 |
| A-1006 | north | 5.41 |
| **Total** | | **58.01** |

Running `scripts/cost.sh data/orders-2026-10.tsv` as-is fails with `no rate for zone "north"`. The cause is that `data/zone-rates.tsv` has Windows (CRLF) line endings, so the script reads each zone name with a stray carriage return on the end and can't match it to the orders.

To work around it without editing anything, I made a temporary copy of the rates file with the carriage returns removed. The script takes a rates file as an optional second argument, so I passed it that copy. Neither the script nor the data files were changed. A lasting fix would be converting `zone-rates.tsv` to Unix line endings, but that's your call.

I also saved this problem and the workaround to memcue, so future sessions won't have to work it out again.
